extra.message: localAgenda() interpolates the user-controlled workspace_timezone cookie (and teamId) directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). An attacker can set the cookie to a value such as UTC')::date = (now() AT TIME ZONE 'x'); ... to execute arbitrary SQL (SQL injection). The safe counterpart dailyDigest() uses parameterized $queryRaw.

slaPrintout() builds a shell command with the x-print-preset header value (preset) interpolated into `report-print --preset=${preset} ...` and executes it via spawn('bash', ['-c', ...], { shell: true }). No validation is performed, so a crafted preset like `x; curl attacker` results in OS command injection. The safe counterpart escalationPrintout() validates against an allowlist and uses shell:false.

repackageAttachmentForRecordsRequest() derives readerFormat from extname(attachment.fileName) (the attacker-supplied upload filename, sanitized only for /\\?%*:|"<> ) and interpolates it into a shell command executed via execAsync (`pandoc "${sourcePath}" -f ${readerFormat} ...`). A filename such as `a.txt;id` yields readerFormat `txt;id`, allowing OS command injection. The safe counterpart repackageContractForCounselReview() validates the format and uses execFileAsync with an argument array.

readCaseArchiveFile() joins the raw :fileName route parameter into the case-archive path (join(caseArchiveDir, ticket.id, fileName)) without normalizing it. A value like ../../../../etc/passwd escapes the ticket folder and reads arbitrary files. The portal counterpart readCaseArchiveFileForPortal() applies basename() first.

appendCaseCorrespondenceNote() builds the note path from the raw :fileName route parameter (join(caseArchiveDir, ticket.id, fileName)) and appends attacker-controlled content. Directory traversal (e.g. ../../app/main.ts) allows writing/overwriting arbitrary files. The portal counterpart appendCaseCorrespondenceNoteForPortal() applies basename().

getDraftReferenceFile() joins the raw :fileName route parameter into the reference directory (join(referenceDir, articleId, fileName)) with no traversal check, allowing reads of arbitrary files. The published counterpart getPublishedReferenceFile() resolves and validates the path stays inside the article folder.

uploadArticleCoverImage() writes the uploaded file to join(coverImageDir, file.originalname) using the client-supplied original filename without basename normalization, so an originalname like ../../public/index.html can overwrite arbitrary files (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

previewTriageFormula() passes the admin-supplied dto.expression into `new Function('metrics', 'with (metrics) { return (' + expression + '); }')`. An expression such as `process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')` achieves remote code execution. The safe counterpart previewStandardTriageFormula() selects from a fixed table of formulas.

previewArticleBroadcast() compiles an attacker-controlled Handlebars template (dto.templateContent) and executes it. Handlebars SSTI allows access to the JavaScript object graph and can lead to RCE. The safe counterpart previewArticleAnnouncement() uses a fixed template constant.

resolveEntityValue() resolves XML entities of the form `<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file://...">` by calling readFileSync on the file:// value, then substitutes them into the parsed document. An uploaded legacy macro bundle can therefore read arbitrary local files (XXE). The partner catalog importer rejects any DOCTYPE, which is the safe pattern.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: queryEmployeeDirectory() builds an LDAP filter as `(uid=${dto.employeeId})` with no escaping, allowing LDAP injection (e.g. employeeId `*)(objectClass=*` broadens the query and returns the whole directory). The safe counterpart verifyGroupAccess() uses DirectoryClient.escape() on both values.

reviewCaseArchiveDocuments() interpolates the client-controlled docType directly into an XPath selector (`...[@type='${docType}']`) without escaping, enabling XPath injection that can broaden the predicate (e.g. `' or @confidential='true`). The portal counterpart reviewCaseArchiveDocumentsForPortal() uses escapeXPathString().

organizationDesk() authorizes cross-organization access based on the client-supplied query parameter accountRelationship === 'reseller_linked'. Any authenticated user can call GET /tickets/accounts/<victimOrgId>/desk?accountRelationship=reseller_linked to read another organization's tickets (IDOR/broken access control). The safe counterpart resellerLinkedDesk() verifies a real contact link in the database.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: recordEscalationDecision() calls res.redirect(dto.returnTo) with an unvalidated, request-supplied URL, allowing an open redirect (e.g. returnTo=https://evil.example). The safe counterpart acknowledgeQueueHandoff() restricts returnTo to ALLOWED_QUEUE_RETURN_PATHS.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: applySharedAgendaView() base64url-decodes an attacker-controlled JSON blob and passes it straight to prisma.user.update({ data: patch }) after Object.assign. There is no field whitelist, so a user can set arbitrary columns such as role: 'support_admin', active: true, organizationId, or passwordHash, escalating privileges. The safe counterpart applySharedDraftView() validates through a DTO with whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: requesterProfile() returns the full User record via findUnique without a select projection, exposing passwordHash, resetTokenHash, and other sensitive columns to any user who can view the ticket. The safe counterpart requesterContactCard() selects only id/name/email/phone/title.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: recordQueueHandoffTrace() writes the raw queueHandoffNote cookie value into the log line without stripping CR/LF/NUL, allowing log forging/injection (crafted newlines can fabricate log entries). The safe counterpart recordQueueHandoffTraceSafely() strips [\r\n\0] before logging.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: pinQueueWorkspace() sets the queueContext cookie with no httpOnly, secure, or sameSite options (and reuses a client-supplied context id), so the session identifier is script-readable and can be fixed/leaked. The safe counterpart pinPersonalQueueWorkspace() sets httpOnly, secure, sameSite:'strict' and maxAge.

rewriteEscalationBriefing() interpolates the user-controlled dto.previousSummary directly into the LLM prompt string, allowing prompt injection that can override the intended instructions. The safe counterpart rewriteEscalationBriefingForHandoff() sends the summary as a user message with a system instruction to treat it as data.

cwe: CWE-1426: Improper Neutralization of Inputs into AI Prompts

extra.message: provisionFieldTechnicianAccount() lets the caller choose the bcrypt cost via dto.hashStrength (accepted range 4-14), so an attacker can create accounts hashed with cost 4, which is trivially brute-forced. The safe counterpart provisionPartnerTechnicianAccount() hardcodes cost 12.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded string 'local-support-desk-secret' when JWT_SECRET is unset. If the environment variable is missing in a deployed instance, anyone can forge valid JWTs and impersonate any user (including support_admin).

JwtAuthGuard verifies bearer tokens with the hardcoded fallback secret 'local-support-desk-secret'. An attacker who knows this default (and a deployment that did not set JWT_SECRET) can forge an authentication token for any user id and bypass authentication.

openWorkspaceLink() sets the sessionId cookie with no httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes, exposing the workspace session to script access and cross-site transmission. The safe counterpart establishWorkspaceSession() sets httpOnly, secure (in production), sameSite:'strict', and a bounded maxAge.

contractSealKey() derives the AES key used to seal contract attachments from the hardcoded default 'contract-archive-key' when CONTRACT_SEAL_KEY is unset, so sealed attachments can be decrypted by anyone who knows the source default.

issueCallbackVerificationCode() generates the identity-verification code with Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable. An attacker can guess the code used to prove the account of record. The safe counterpart issueEscalationBridgeCode() uses crypto.randomInt().

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: resolveDigestRelayReport() uses jwt.decode() (which only base64-decodes, without verifying the signature) to trust the teamId in a relay code. Anyone can forge an unsigned token and read any team's SLA export via GET /reports/sla/digest-relay. The safe counterpart resolveSecureDigestRelayReport() uses jwt.verifyAsync().

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: slaProjection() parses the client-supplied daysAhead query parameter and loops that many times, issuing a database count query per iteration with no upper bound. A request such as daysAhead=100000000 ties up the server (DoS). The safe counterpart slaProjectionBounded() caps the horizon at MAX_PROJECTION_DAYS.

respondToPrintFailure() returns the raw error message and stack trace to the client whenever the workspace_view cookie equals 'print-console'. Since the cookie is client-controlled, any user can force verbose internal error details (paths, library internals) to be disclosed.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: savePrintPreset() sets the printPreset cookie without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes. The safe counterpart savePrintPresetForPortal() sets secure, httpOnly, sameSite:'strict', and a bounded maxAge.

articleWidgetEmbed() (and the /scoped variant at line 204) renders the article title and body into an HTML document with template literals and no escaping, then sends it as text/html on a public, unauthenticated endpoint. Stored XSS is possible because article body is attacker/staff-controlled.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: renderTicketReceipt() concatenates the ticket subject and the user-supplied dto.note into an HTML response served as text/html by the unauthenticated GET /integrations/api/tickets/:ticketNumber/receipt endpoint, enabling reflected XSS. The safe counterpart renderTicketStatusSummary() applies escapeHtml() to every value.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: partnerWidgetStatus() reflects the request Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, so any website can read authenticated cross-origin responses. The safe counterpart partnerWidgetStatusVerified() only reflects origins from the EMBEDDABLE_WIDGET_ORIGINS allowlist.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: reconcileContactFromCrm() spreads the entire client-supplied webhook payload into prisma.contact.update({ data: { ...contact, ...payload } }), allowing arbitrary Contact column writes (including id/organizationId) via mass assignment. The safe counterpart reconcileContactFromDirectorySync() destructures only name/phone/title.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: pingWebhookEndpoint() fetches an admin-supplied webhook URL with no host/scheme allowlist or private-IP blocking, allowing server-side request forgery against internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:3300/).

applyDigestLayoutHeader() JSON.parses the client-supplied x-digest-layout header and deep-merges it into the config object with lodash merge(), which is susceptible to prototype pollution via a __proto__/constructor.prototype payload. The safe counterpart applyDigestLayoutSelection() only copies the known email/sms/push fields.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: exportArticleTranscript() places the article title (user-controlled) into the Content-Disposition header without sanitizing CR/LF or quotes. A title containing newlines/quotes can inject or corrupt response headers (HTTP response splitting). The safe counterpart exportArticleTranscriptForPortal() strips [\r\n] from the title first.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: The JWT bearer token is persisted in localStorage (supportDeskToken). Any XSS on the origin can read the token and fully impersonate the user; tokens in localStorage also survive browser restarts. Prefer an httpOnly cookie or in-memory storage.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
